intended_object: The canonical topology on an algebraic extension M of a nonarchimedean local field K: the topology induced by the unique absolute value on M that extends the absolute value of K, which is the spectral norm. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body takes the topology underlying the uniform space of `algebraicExtensionNormedField K M`. That normed field is Mathlib's `spectralNorm.normedField K M`, built after putting the normalized absolute value on K, which is complete and ultrametric. So this is exactly the topology of the spectral norm. That is the standard topology on an algebraic extension of a local field: it is the unique extension of the absolute value (Neukirch II.4.8).

The file backs this up. `algebraicExtension_isValuativeTopology` shows the topology is the valuative topology of the extended valuation. `algebraicExtensionNormedFieldTopology_eq` shows it agrees with any valuative topology on M whose valuative relation extends that of K. So there is no degenerate-case problem.

On generality: the general construction for complete ultrametric normed fields already exists in Mathlib (`spectralNorm.normedField`), and this definition only applies it. The local-field setting is still needed here. In this library K carries a `ValuativeRel` and a topology but no norm. The norm has to be produced by `normalizedNontriviallyNormedField K`, and that construction uses the local-field structure (the normalized absolute value). Mathlib has no named definition for the topology of the spectral norm, so the definition is a reasonable wrapper at its natural generality.
